title: Job 24
paragraphs: ¹ Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why do those who know him never see his days of reckoning? ² There are those who move boundary stones; they steal flocks and pasture them for themselves. ³ They drive off the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow's ox as a pledge. ⁴ They shove the needy off the road; the poor of the land are all forced into hiding. ⁵ Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go about their labor of scavenging food; the wasteland provides for their children.

⁶ They harvest grain in the fields of others; they glean in the vineyards of the wicked. ⁷ They spend the night naked, without clothing, and have no covering in the cold. ⁸ Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks with no shelter. ⁹ The fatherless child is snatched from the breast; the infant of the poor is taken as a pledge. ¹⁰ They go about naked, lacking clothing; hungry, they carry another man's sheaves.

¹¹ They press out oil among the olive terraces; they tread the winepresses while they themselves go thirsty. ¹² In the city the dying groan; the wounded cry out for help — but God charges no one with wrongdoing. ¹³ There are those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways or stay in its paths. ¹⁴ The murderer rises before dawn to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief. ¹⁵ The eye of the adulterer watches for dusk; he thinks, 'No eye will see me,' and keeps his face covered.

¹⁶ In the dark they break into houses; by day they shut themselves in, wanting nothing to do with the light. ¹⁷ For deep darkness is their morning; they are friends with the terrors of the darkness. ¹⁸ He is swift as foam on the water; their portion of the land is cursed, and no one turns toward their vineyards. ¹⁹ As drought and heat snatch away the snow, so the grave takes away those who have sinned. ²⁰ The womb forgets them; the worm devours them; they are remembered no more. Wickedness is broken like a tree.

²¹ He preys on the childless woman who has no son and brings no good to the widow. ²² Yet God, by his power, drags away the mighty; they may rise, but no one can be sure of their life. ²³ Though God gives them security, they rest in it — yet his eyes are always on their ways. ²⁴ They are exalted for a little while, then they are gone — brought low, gathered up like everything else, cut down like heads of grain.
